en.html:
Almost empty, my body's caloric reserves. Ordinarily the cure was simple. Khao, phir so jao. Easily digested food, at least six hours' sleep. The body had these requirements. It was not interested in my opinion of them.

At present, however, speed took priority over proper condition. Give the magistrate time and his position could recover. He had received a blow; perhaps he still had not understood the situation fully. Pursue now, while understanding was catching up. Otherwise time's advantage would change sides, and nobody would ask my permission.

A general store tucked away in the village. Two or three preserved foods selected and put into the stomach. Light exercise for digestion. Then defecation. Then a little rest.

Kul milaake: two hours.

A magnificent imitation of recovery. Better than nothing, bas. That was the full extent of it.

Proper meal lene ki takleef nahin ki, now on what basis would I complain? For a short fight, this much should suffice. I would have to keep the fight short, therefore. The stomach had already settled its part of the strategy.

ja.html:
代官との一戦は、体内の<ruby>熱量<rt>カロリー</rt></ruby>をほぼ限度まで奪って
いた。通常、この消耗を補うには食事と休息のほかに
方法がない。消化の良いものを摂取し、六時間以上の
睡眠を取る必要があった。

　しかし現状、迅速な行動は体調の確保に優先する。
代官に時間を与え、巻き返しを許すべきではなかった。
彼が打撃を受け、おそらくは状況把握もまだ不十分で
あろう今の間に追撃せねば、時の利を失う。

　村の奥まった一角で見つけた雑貨屋で、保存食料の
類を二、三みつくろって腹へ収め、軽く体を動かして
消化を促し、脱糞した後少し休む。
　都合二時間。

　何もしないよりはましという程度の補給にしかなら
なかったが、まともな食事を得る手間を惜しんだのだ
から仕方がない。
　この程度でも短時間の戦闘には耐える筈だ。

en.html:
I walked a road whose paving had not received full commitment. No villagers in sight. Perhaps the fields were in another direction. Perhaps, after the disturbance, everyone was keeping indoors. Or perhaps evening was reason enough. The sun was already in the western sky.

I wanted the matter settled before night. Wanting was one thing. Whether it would happen—difficult, perhaps.

Deep autumn already. The season when the sun drops like a bucket into a well. No lingering over the descent.

en.html:
Foolish thought.

Apni jaan ka bharosa nahin, and I proposed bringing somebody else along. 'Please guide me through the forest. If we meet the enemy, your safety I cannot guarantee. Such assistance will be appreciated.'

How would that be permissible? Difficulty had apparently begun making me weak.

I pressed my left fingernails into my right palm. A little pain. Enough to call the mind back to its duty.

en.html:
Her sulky metal-echo arrived directly inside my ears as I threaded through the trees. We should not have been very deep in the forest yet. Still, which way we had come, which way we were going—both information now missing. Tree. More tree. The previous tree might have been useful as a landmark if all its neighbours had not been doing the same thing.

In morning sunlight, perhaps a pleasant walk. At this hour, with darkness nearly here, an onlooker would probably take it for a test of courage. Or a wish to die.

The latter was more likely. Every tree seemed to have a suitable branch for hanging something.

My foot caught on something. A root, apparently washed bare by the rain.

I checked my shoe. Undamaged. Proceed. Some care was required here. An injury was unlikely, but break a shoe and my movement would be finished.

A warrior and a demon tsurugi, stopped by inadequate footwear. The enemy would be entitled to laugh. I preferred not to provide him with an entirely justified pleasure.

en.html:
...The bad prediction proved correct. These predictions were usually very reliable.

Someone was there. Back toward us, medium height, school uniform. A youth from the village, perhaps? Crouching with arms around their legs, facing something.

Something.
An ordinary animal would have been hidden behind that figure from where we stood. This one, no difficulty seeing it at all. Ordinary was therefore already ruled out.

A dog. Probably a mountain dog. The menacing eyes and rough coat put it well apart from the dogs found around human homes. One of those dangerous roamers of the wild, apparently—the ones people nowadays called "the Honourable Government" to mock Rokuhara.

But this body. Arre. It seemed as large as a small bear. On its hind legs, would it not stand almost as tall as a human? Even the most modest description would have to admit: not a normal dog.

en.html: An animal of that size could probably be dealt with without armour. But that was not the meaning of my reply. I slowed my run, quieted my footsteps and approached. Come crashing in, startle the person, and the beast might seize its chance. Unnecessary assistance was bad enough. Unnecessary assistance that made everything worse—no, thank you. I stopped some distance away and concealed myself behind a suitable tree. The mountain dog, however, had probably noticed the new arrival. Perhaps it judged that the situation had changed. One shrill bark, like a final warning—◆¦and before its echo faded, the animal bared its fangs and launched itself at the figure, still motionless, almost indifferent. Fast. Not a cat's movement. The direct, sharp-angled rush of a dog. Given enough distance, perhaps one could evade it. From this close, hardly. At last, the figure was getting up. That unhurried lifting of the head looked more like a bear's movement than anything the huge dog was doing. Much slower. Almost sluggish. The dog rushed. The figure rose. —Contact. And in that instant, the one whose intention succeeded was not the monster-dog that had raced several ken to reach a human throat.
en.text:
An animal of that size could probably be dealt with without armour. But that was not the meaning of my reply.

I slowed my run, quieted my footsteps and approached. Come crashing in, startle the person, and the beast might seize its chance.

Unnecessary assistance was bad enough. Unnecessary assistance that made everything worse—no, thank you. I stopped some distance away and concealed myself behind a suitable tree.

The mountain dog, however, had probably noticed the new arrival. Perhaps it judged that the situation had changed. One shrill bark, like a final warning—◆¦and before its echo faded, the animal bared its fangs and launched itself at the figure, still motionless, almost indifferent.

Fast. Not a cat's movement. The direct, sharp-angled rush of a dog. Given enough distance, perhaps one could evade it. From this close, hardly.

At last, the figure was getting up.

That unhurried lifting of the head looked more like a bear's movement than anything the huge dog was doing. Much slower. Almost sluggish.

The dog rushed.
The figure rose.

—Contact.

And in that instant, the one whose intention succeeded was not the monster-dog that had raced several ken to reach a human throat.

手頃な木の陰に身を隠す。

en.html:
First contact: right fist, mountain dog's throat. The force was the dog's own. Fist wahaan rakh diya, bas. Put it in that place. Everything else, the animal supplied. I thought I heard a brief, odd sound. Perhaps imagined. The cry that followed, and the enormous dog flying backward like an unwilling acrobat, drove other thoughts away for a moment. It fell near its starting place. The student finished standing and walked toward it. Its movements were weakening already. Mar raha tha. Dying. That tremendous strength had produced its own ending. At least suffering had been short. Seen that way, an irony. Pitiable, though. Finish it? Perhaps that was the question. The approaching step faltered. During the hesitation, the matter ended by itself. Last breath gone. Forest quiet again. Even from behind, the bitterness in that figure was visible. Seeing that back, I—
Choices
  • Straightforward, I think.
  • Immature, I think.
en.text:
First contact: right fist, mountain dog's throat. The force was the dog's own.

Fist wahaan rakh diya, bas. Put it in that place. Everything else, the animal supplied.

I thought I heard a brief, odd sound. Perhaps imagined. The cry that followed, and the enormous dog flying backward like an unwilling acrobat, drove other thoughts away for a moment. It fell near its starting place.

The student finished standing and walked toward it. Its movements were weakening already. Mar raha tha. Dying.

That tremendous strength had produced its own ending. At least suffering had been short. Seen that way, an irony. Pitiable, though.

Finish it? Perhaps that was the question. The approaching step faltered. During the hesitation, the matter ended by itself.

Last breath gone. Forest quiet again. Even from behind, the bitterness in that figure was visible.

Seeing that back, I—

Choices
• Straightforward, I think.
• Immature, I think.

いるかのように宙へ舞い、弧を描きつつ元の位置まで
転げ落ちていく大柄な山犬の姿は、一瞬、忘我を避け

　落ちた犬が、のたうつ――激しく、短く。
　学生服の人物が完全に立ち上がり、犬の傍まで歩み
寄った頃には、既にその四肢の痙攣は弱いものとなり、
か細く末期の息を洩らすばかりになっていた。

　一撃は喉ばかりでなく、頚骨まで砕いたのだろう。

に済んだ――そう思えば皮肉であり、哀れであった。

近付く足がふと、たたらを踏む。

静寂が戻る。そして人影の背には後味の悪さが滲んだ。
